card.title: Nintendo Switch BQ24193 Charging IC Test Procedure and Voltage Checks

claims.statement: When checking the BQ24193 chip with a charger plugged into the switch, Pin 1 VBus should be high 5v-15v depending on the charger.
claims.evidence: Check the voltages on BQ24193 Pin 1 VBus should be high 5v-15v depending on charger
claims.quote: Pin 1 VBus should be high 5v-15v depending on charger

claims.statement: Pin 2 of the BQ24193 should read low if using the Nintendo charger.
claims.evidence: Voltage check on pin 2 using official charger.
claims.quote: pin 2 if using the nintendo charger this pin should read low

claims.statement: Pin 3 of the BQ24193 should be low at 0v.
Pin 4 of the BQ24193 should be low if charge is in progress, high if charge is complete or disabled, and alternating if there is a fault.
claims.evidence: Voltage check on pin 4 during charging states.
claims.quote: pin 4 should be low if charge in progress, if this pin is high charge is complete or disabled, if this pin is alternating from low to high this could indicate a fault.

procedure: {'step': 'Expose copper on the battery connector cables for the 5 cables (2 red, 1 grey, 2 black).'}
{'step': 'Set multimeter to DC voltage, place negative probe on one of the black cables, and read voltage on the first and second red cables.'}
{'step': 'Plug the battery back in, leave the switch charging for 30 minutes without touching the power button.'}
{'step': 'Unplug the charger, unplug the battery, and recheck the red cable voltages; if higher than before, the console is charging and the BQ24193 is fine.'}
{'step': 'If it did not charge at all, the BQ24193 may be dead and you should check the BQ24193 pin voltages.'}
card.caveats: If pin 4 is alternating from low to high, it could indicate a fault rather than a normal charging state.
